title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The AI Office has issued a formal decision that sets out how artificial intelligence should be managed within the organization. It establishes clear rules and responsibilities for using AI safely and responsibly.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: This policy announces a job opening for technology specialists in AI within the office. It outlines the duties, required qualifications, and application process for the position.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: The policy announces an open position for a Lead Scientific Adviser in the AI office, outlining the role’s responsibilities, required expertise, and expected contributions to AI research and strategy. It also describes the selection process, reporting structure, and the adviser’s role in shaping the office’s scientific priorities and ethical standards.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: The policy explains how the organization will handle vacant positions for Legal Officers who oversee AI projects. It sets guidelines for hiring, duties, and compliance to ensure these roles meet legal and ethical standards.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: This policy outlines the roles and responsibilities of Policy Officers in the AI Office. It explains how these officers will develop, implement, and oversee AI policies to ensure ethical and responsible use of artificial intelligence.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group tasked with examining the scientific and technical implications of AI regulations. Their findings guide policymakers in shaping effective, evidence‑based AI legislation.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: This draft outlines a preliminary request to establish standardized practices for AI development and deployment. It seeks consistent guidelines on safety, transparency, and accountability to ensure reliable and ethical use of AI technologies.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: The CoP Consultation Notice is an announcement that a new or revised policy will be opened for public discussion. It invites stakeholders to review the draft and submit their feedback by a specified deadline.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: This notice invites people to show interest in joining a Community of Practice (CoP) focused on AI policy. It explains what the CoP will work on and how you can submit an expression of interest.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: This policy document presents a graphic that outlines the iterative drafting process used within the community of practice. It visually explains how ideas are refined through repeated cycles of review, feedback, and revision to develop clearer, more effective policies.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: The document is a visual timeline that illustrates the step-by-step process involved in drafting the AI policy. It highlights key milestones, deadlines, and decision points to help stakeholders understand the development schedule.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: The “Code of Practice: 1st Draft” is an initial guide outlining responsible ways to develop, deploy, and use artificial intelligence. It sets out basic rules and best‑practice recommendations to help organizations manage AI risks and ensure ethical, safe, and transparent AI systems.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: This document presents the second draft of a Code of Practice for the responsible development and use of AI, aiming to guide stakeholders in creating trustworthy systems. It outlines key principles, best practices, and compliance requirements to promote ethical, transparent, and safe AI deployment across industries.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: The third draft of the Code of Practice sets out a framework of guidelines intended to govern the ethical development and deployment of artificial intelligence. It stresses transparency, fairness, and accountability, aiming to help organizations adopt responsible AI practices.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft proposes a collaborative framework to guide responsible AI development, stressing transparency, accountability, and public trust. It offers guidelines for stakeholders to align AI innovations with societal values and to address risks like bias, privacy concerns, and potential misuse.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final outlines a comprehensive framework for responsible AI development and deployment, emphasizing transparency, fairness, and accountability across industries. It sets forth commitments by stakeholders to prioritize human rights, mitigate bias, and establish governance mechanisms to ensure AI systems align with societal values.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: This policy lists AI behaviors that are strictly prohibited, such as creating deceptive deepfakes, making biased or discriminatory decisions, or using AI for harmful or illegal purposes. It explains why those actions are disallowed and the rules for enforcing the restrictions.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: The document explains how to identify and classify AI systems, outlining the features and criteria that make a system qualify as AI. It provides rules and guidelines for developers and organizations to determine whether a particular software or service falls under the AI system definition for regulatory and compliance purposes.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This policy outlines strategies for communicating with and supporting start-ups to foster innovation, emphasizing the importance of clear, consistent messaging across platforms. It encourages collaboration between government, industry, and academia to create a supportive ecosystem that accelerates technological development and market growth.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start‑Ups is a European program that gives early‑stage technology companies access to high‑performance computing resources, training, and support to speed up their product development. It also connects start‑ups with research institutions and funding bodies to foster collaboration and help bring innovative solutions to market.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar presents a slideshow overview of risk management, outlining key concepts and practical strategies. Viewers will learn how to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across different scenarios and industries.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: The webinar covers how to identify, assess, and mitigate risks associated with AI systems. It emphasizes best practices for governance, monitoring, and continuous improvement to keep AI operations safe and ethical.
